name: Concrete leveling drop-servicing
one_liner: Sell concrete lifting and leveling jobs to homeowners and pass all the physical work to subcontractors, keeping the margin.
customer: Homeowners and property owners with sunken or uneven driveways, patios and sidewalks
offer: Concrete leveling/lifting (polyjacking/mudjacking), sold and managed by you and done by subcontracted crews
how_it_makes_money: You charge per job (example jobs of $800 and $9,000) and keep a 30-40% gross margin after paying the subcontractor
startup_cost: low (no equipment or employees; marketing and lead-gen spend only, amount not stated)
time_to_first_revenue: weeks; nearly $20K profit soon after starting, with $100K profit expected in the first 6 months
evidence: '30 to 40% gross margin on each job'; target of $250K revenue this year, $1M next year (QTWNnonldjw)
Founder has a W-2 job, no employees, subcontracts everything (QTWNnonldjw)
risks: Very US-centric; demand for slab lifting and the contractor supply in the UK need checking
Liability and quality control rest with you while the work is done by others
Needs site visits for quotes unless you use photo-based quoting
Saturated in big metros

name: Mailbox install & repair
one_liner: Local service that replaces and repairs leaning or rusty mailboxes, with upsells to novelty mailboxes and HOA contracts.
offer: Mailbox replacement, repair, painting and custom/novelty mailboxes
how_it_makes_money: Per-install pricing at a claimed 90%+ gross margin, plus bulk HOA contracts 'worth tens of thousands'
time_to_first_revenue: days; one operator made $9,000+ in a single week door-knocking
evidence: 'one guy made over $9,000 in a single week just by walking around his neighborhood with some paint and a shovel' (R6-Es5rLfuA)
'start with a hundred bucks'; '90 plus% gross profit margins' (R6-Es5rLfuA)
A dog-shaped mailbox seller on Facebook grew into a profitable business (R6-Es5rLfuA)
risks: UK homes mostly have letterboxes in the door, not curbside posts, so the market barely exists there
Physical, local work
Hard to scale beyond one operator

name: Liquidation pallet/truckload reselling
one_liner: Buy returns and overstock pallets or truckloads at 2-5 cents on the dollar and resell them at 20-30 cents.
customer: Online and local bargain buyers, bin stores, smaller resellers
offer: Resold liquidation goods, either by item or in lots
how_it_makes_money: Buy-low/sell-high arbitrage: about a 4-10x markup on cost (2-5¢ in, 20-30¢ out per $ of retail)
startup_cost: low-medium (one example: a $28K deal that sold for $103K; a truckload for under $4K)
evidence: 'He'll buy them for 2 to 5 cents on the dollar and sell them for 20 to 30 cents on the dollar' (QYRz3WgE7eY)
'We bought the deal for $28,000 and sold it for 103. We did it in our garage' (QYRz3WgE7eY)
risks: Needs storage space and handling time
Pallet quality is uneven
UK liquidation supply is smaller than the US (Jobalots and B-Stock UK exist)

name: Luxury handbag resale
one_liner: Source pre-owned luxury handbags, authenticate them, and resell them online.
how_it_makes_money: Margin on each bag; one operator sold $4M over 3 years and netted $557K (~14%)
time_to_first_revenue: weeks; he spent about a year learning the category
evidence: 'I just by myself sold about $4 million worth of handbags. Made $557,000 net profit' (QYRz3WgE7eY)
risks: Counterfeits and authentication liability
High capital per item
Long learning curve

name: College-town furniture/couch flipping
one_liner: Collect free or cheap couches, clean them, photograph them well, and resell them, timed around the student move-in and move-out cycle.
customer: Students, parents and shared households in university towns
how_it_makes_money: Profit on each flip from items picked up free or cheap; seasonal peaks at term start
evidence: A member 'picks up free couches from Facebook Marketplace... cleans them up... and sells them' (OZ0fdAYPyqE)
'if you live in a college town, you should be in the couch business' (OZ0fdAYPyqE)
risks: UK furniture fire-safety labelling rules for resale
Bulky items need transport and storage
Low ceiling

name: Weekend wood-fired pizza trailer/events
one_liner: Sell artisan pizza from a trailer or pop-up at weekend events and markets.
customer: Event-goers, private parties, weddings, local markets
offer: Wood-fired pizzas at $15-20 each, plus event catering
how_it_makes_money: Per-pizza sales at 60-90% margin on ingredients, plus event booking fees
startup_cost: medium (oven and trailer; started small and bought kit gradually)
evidence: 'sells authentic Italian pizzas for $15 to $20 each'; 'roughly 60% profit' (OWhPtx1SAWg)
A UK professor 'making $175,000 in net profit slanging pizzas on the weekend' with two ovens in a trailer (OWhPtx1SAWg)
risks: Fully in-person; weekends are taken
Food hygiene registration and council licensing
Weather and how often events run

name: AI PR outreach tool for small businesses
one_liner: Vibe-coded SaaS or done-for-you service that finds relevant journalists, writes personalised pitches and tracks replies.
customer: Small businesses and new launches that can't afford a PR agency
offer: Automated journalist discovery, AI pitch writing, sending and open/reply tracking
how_it_makes_money: Subscription priced against a PR hire costing 'about 20, 30, 40 bucks a month'
startup_cost: low (Bolt or Claude Code plus API costs)
evidence: Weak: a built-in-an-hour demo with no revenue shown; framed as replacing a PR person for '20, 30, 40 bucks a month' (OomOCuptgr4)
risks: No demand evidence
Email deliverability, spam and GDPR/PECR rules on cold outreach in the UK
Crowded space with low willingness to pay
